producer_report.summary:
Athena's own improvement requests (the Steward's and Hestia's) now get a guaranteed turn in the drain, and a request whose cause is in three or more distinct jobs counts as urgent.

**Root cause.** The drain ordered by priority alone, so a person's urgent and high requests always sorted ahead of Athena's own requests.

**How it works.** `Plan::build_improving` in `plan.rs` wraps `build_capped`.
- It raises a request whose cause is in three or more distinct jobs to urgent, in memory only. This happens before `[priority_caps]`, so a full urgent tier can demote it again. A priority a person set is never changed.
- It then walks the order once. While a ready improvement request is queued, at most two other items run in a row. The best-ranked ready one moves into the place that is due.
- A request that is refused, held, or has an unmet dependency is skipped. The skipped request is never a candidate.
- A moved request becomes a group of its own, so a parallel wave cannot start ahead of it.
- `priority_violations` no longer reports a moved request as a priority contradiction.
- With no improvement item among the entries, the result is exactly the `build_capped` result.

**Which requests count.** `hestia::improvement_of` finds them by recorded links, never by title:
- open requests on the `steward` channel (`steward::improvement_requests`);
- the open request that cites a repeated cause's introspections, together with the number of distinct jobs for that cause;
- the `request_job` of a throughput proposal;
- the open request holding a `Spec requirement: <id>` line, using a helper shared with `spec_request_is_open`.

The throughput slowdown request is not covered, because no record links it.

**Drain.** `Steps::improvement()` is a new default method. The drain counts consecutive other dispatches (`since_turn`) so each replan after a dispatch keeps the gap. The report gains `improvement_turns`.

**Display.** `athena plan` prints a `turn` line for each turn and a `promoted` line for each raised request, with the demotion that followed if there was one. `athena drain` prints an `improvement` line for each turn taken. The help text of both commands is updated.

**Tests added.**
- Six urgent requests plus two Steward requests: a Steward request is within the first three, at positions 3 and 6.
- A cause in three distinct jobs is urgent; in two it is not, and a person-set priority is never changed.
- With no improvement requests, the result equals `build_capped`.
- Refused, held and unready requests get no turn.
- The plan text names each turn, and the drain report lists them.
- Run order equals the printed plan order.
- Under `drain_concurrent`, a Steward request starts among the first three.

I did not touch `athena.toml`, `defaults.toml`, the two-job filing threshold, or the caps.

criteria_check.evidence: plan.rs `build_improving` walks `plan.order`, which holds only planned entries, so a refused or held id is never a candidate. open_issues: The throughput slowdown request gets no guaranteed turn. No record links it: only its title prefix and the free text of the review note identify it. Covering it needs a job field on `ThroughputReview`, which changes records and filing and is out of scope. It is named as not covered in the `improvement_of` doc comment and the CHANGELOG, and a hestia.rs test asserts it is not listed.

The three-job promotion is made before `[priority_caps]`, as the plan decided. When person-set urgent items fill the urgent tier, a promoted request is demoted to high. The `promoted` line in `athena plan` shows this, and a plan.rs test covers it. The guaranteed turn still applies in that case.

A person's own request that cites a repeated cause's introspection ids, or holds a `Spec requirement:` line, counts as an improvement request, because the link is by citation and not by author. This is stated in the doc comment and the CHANGELOG.

mistakes: My first version of the order-check test swapped the first and last places. That did not create a violation, because the moved item is skipped as the earlier item. I rewrote it to move a normal item to the front.
I tried a cargo test filter with two test paths, which cargo rejected; I reran it with the filters after `--`.
learnings: The Steward channel marker alone misses Hestia: every Hestia request is queued on channel `cli`. So `improvement_of` finds Hestia's requests by their recorded links: the `RepeatedCause.request` link, `ThroughputProposal.request_job`, and the `Spec requirement:` body line.
`build_capped` ranks tiers by each entry's own priority, not its effective priority. A promotion has to be applied to the entries before `build_capped` for the caps to see it.
`batches_for` puts items with no plan entry ahead of planned ones. They still advance `since_turn`, so the next planned dispatch is the improvement turn.
Under `drain_concurrent` a whole plan group starts at once. A moved turn item therefore has to be its own group, or a group of six independent urgent items would still start ahead of it.
`cargo test -p xtask --test policy` and `-p athena-cli --test mirrors` both pass; neither needed a timings-file edit because no test file was added.
